question: Should OpenClaw core own a private TaskFlow-based orchestration layer for separate Pi and Review services, including a vendored contracts runtime dependency?
rationale: The patch adds a new cross-service Core responsibility and dependency model rather than repairing an established OpenClaw behavior; code review cannot determine whether that product and ownership boundary is intended.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core design
options.body: Approve the Core ownership boundary, require secops review of the exact vendored artifact, and ask for a self-contained test plus live durability proof before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Keep orchestration outside core
options.body: Decline the new Core seam and move the workflow and contracts ownership to the service or owner repository that operates Pi and Review.

options.title: Pause pending architecture discussion
options.body: Leave the PR open only while an owner documents the intended public and operational boundary for the involved services.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core design
recommendation.body: Approve the Core ownership boundary, require secops review of the exact vendored artifact, and ask for a self-contained test plus live durability proof before reconsidering merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The immediate merge gate is the exact-head security and dependency authorization for files assigned to this review group; product sponsorship should be coordinated with that review.
